newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Aegon up 18.5 pct in 1996 after strong Q4.
newsitem.headline: Aegon up 18.5 pct in 1996 after strong Q4.

text.p: Dutch insurer Aegon said Friday its net profit rose 18.5 percent to 1.57 billion guilders ($825 million) in 1996 from 1.32 billion ($694 million) in 1995 after an exceptionally strong fourth quarter performance.
It raised its dividend to 2.79 guilders from 2.37 and forecast a further rise in profits of 10 percent to 12 percent in 1997.
Aegon said this forecast excluded a further positive effect on earnings that it expected from the acquisition of U.S. company Providian Corp.'s insurance activities.
Aegon announced the $3.5 billion Providian takeover -- the biggest by a Dutch company to date -- in December and expects to close the deal in the first half of this year.
"The acquisition of Providian Corporation's insurance activities will have a further positive impact on Aegon's earnings per share," it said.
Aegon said buoyant stock markets and an exceptionally strong fourth quarter helped lift its full-year earnings.

"The full year's net income showed a higher than expected increase, due to an exceptionally good fourth quarter operationally, favourable stock market conditions and the strengthening of Aegon's main currencies," it said.
Aegon said it had achieved double-digit growth of pre-tax profits in all four of its main business areas in 1996.
Life insurance posted a 15 percent rise, accident and health insurance profits were up 13 percent, general insurance earnings advanced 61 percent while banking profits rose 16 percent.
Aegon said 1996 earnings were boosted in part by the appreciation of the dollar and sterling against the guilder, particularly in the final quarter of the year.
U.S. earnings rose 14.2 percent in dollars but 20 percent in guilders. Earnings of Aegon's Scottish Equitable unit grew 24 percent in sterling terms.
Aegon chairman Kees Storm described 1996 as a year of high-quality growth, adding that he was confident 1997 would be another good year.

"Through well considered acquisitions and divestments we further focused our portfolio on our core businesses. But most importantly we managed to maintain solid organic growth in all our major markets," he said.
On the Amsterdam bourse Aegon shares were up 2.10 guilders at 131.00 ($68.83) in afternoon trading, a rise of 1.6 percent compared with a rise of 2.5 percent for the main AEX stock market index.
Aegon's full-year profit was just outside the upper end of analysts' forecasts of 1.535 billion to 1.567 billion guilders ($807 million to $823 million).
